etymologies.etymologyHTML: From commit +‎ -ee, or else revival of Anglo-Norman commite, past participle of commettre (“to commit”), from Latin committere, from con- (“with”) + mittere (“to send”). The OED3 prefers the first etymology.

definitions.definition: A body of one or more persons convened for the accomplishment of some specific purpose, typically with formal protocols.
(archaic) A guardian; someone in charge of another person deemed to be unable to look after themselves.
(Pakistan, British Pakistani, finance) Alternative form of kameti
